question: Should OpenClaw accept this PR as the canonical opt-in durable runtime core for the staged durable stack, including its SQLite schema, env knobs, and gateway/operator surfaces?
rationale: The patch appears technically coherent and well-covered, but it introduces persistent state, default policy, recovery behavior, and operator APIs whose acceptance is a product and upgrade-safety decision rather than an automation-repairable defect.

options.title: Gate on PR1 and upgrade proof
options.body: Resolve the PR1/base stack, keep durable runtime default-off, and require fresh-install plus upgrade validation for the SQLite schema and env defaults before merge.

options.title: Accept the experimental core risk
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally accept the opt-in durable state, config, recovery, and operator support burden as an experimental core capability.

options.title: Pause the durable stack
options.body: If PR1 is not the canonical boundary, pause or close this PR and restart implementation from the accepted durable-runtime direction.

recommendation.title: Gate on PR1 and upgrade proof
recommendation.body: Resolve the PR1/base stack, keep durable runtime default-off, and require fresh-install plus upgrade validation for the SQLite schema and env defaults before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Frank is the listed routing owner for PR triage, Agents, Gateway, and Channels, which best matches this cross-cutting durable runtime acceptance decision.
